newsitem.title: USA: Ashland, Marathon see benefits without closures.
newsitem.headline: Ashland, Marathon see benefits without closures.

text.p: Ashland Inc and USX Corp's Marathon Oil Co expect substantial benefits from their proposed refining venture, USX Corp said Thursday.
These efficiencies are not premised on the closure of major operating facilities, it stressed.

However, as the new company structure is formed, there will likely be workforce reductions and job reassignments, but the long-term growth potential of this combined entity could provide future employment opportunities, USX said. Marathon Oil is part of USX'S USX-Marathon Group.

Marathon and Ashland have agreed to pursue a combinination of their downstream -- refining, marketing and transportation -- activities into a new company owned 62 percent by Marathon and 38 percent by Ashland.

Marathon's four refinieries have a total capacity of 575,000 barrels daily, 3.7 percent of U.S. capacity, while Ashland's three can consume up to 355,000 barrels of crude daily, or 2.3 percent of the nation's total.
The two companies already have a jointly owned light product terminal in Niles, Mich, USX said.

Marathon has 51 light product and asphalt terminals in the Midwest and Southeast, and markets through 3,980 outlets in 17 states. Ashland owns 34 terminals and 1,400 outlets in 11 mostly Midwestern states. Both have outlets in Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio, Vierginia and West Virginia.
"The goal of this joint venture is to create a competitive enterprise which capitalizes on the strengths and complementary assets of both companies," USX Chairman Thomas J. Usher said.
"Market conditions have dictated that new approaches be explored to improve performance and growth opportunities."

Ashland Chief Executive Paul Chellgren added, "The petroleum refining and marketing industry in the United States is undergoing a rapid transformation based on the need to improve profitability, create new efficiencies and better serve customers and shareholders."
Usher and Chellgren emphasized that prospective synergies will be defined over the next several months.

It is expected the venture will be able to achieve substantial benefits largely by pursuing operational efficiencies and integrating the strengths of their business processes, management systems and administrative support functions, USX said.
It also said future decisions on the closure of operating facilities will be governed by business conditions and the needs of the venture.
